questions.question: A model scores 90% on recall questions, but the product claim promises reliable troubleshooting. What evidence is still required?
options: Only more recall questions from the same source
Application items that represent new troubleshooting cases and critical failure slices
A larger font for the score
Removal of all incorrect outputs
questions.explanation: Recall breadth does not establish transfer. The suite needs representative application tasks and enough evidence in decision-critical troubleshooting slices.

questions.question: Why should an evaluation blueprint be fixed before final model results are inspected?
options: It prevents the item mix from being changed to favor observed strengths
It guarantees every item is uncontaminated
It removes the need for slice analysis
It makes all domains equally important
questions.explanation: Predeclaring coverage reduces result-driven benchmark composition. Provenance, item quality, and uncertainty still require separate controls.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes closed-book and open-book knowledge evaluation?
options: They measure exactly the same system behavior
Open book is always easier and therefore invalid
Closed book probes answers without supplied evidence, while open book tests the system's ability to find and use provided evidence
Closed book never requires a scoring protocol
questions.explanation: The access mode changes the object being evaluated. Results must identify whether retrieval, context, or tools were available.

questions.question: A critical source-use slice has 32 items and 84% observed accuracy. Why might a release gate still block the claim?
options: Observed accuracy is never useful
The slice may miss the minimum item count or uncertainty-aware lower-bound threshold
Critical slices should be excluded from the report
Only the aggregate score can be gated
questions.explanation: A high point estimate from a thin slice can have weak lower-bound evidence. Critical claims need predeclared sample and uncertainty requirements.

questions.question: What should happen when prompt sensitivity and contamination have not been checked?
options: Treat both values as zero
Infer them from aggregate accuracy
Record them as unknown and investigate before expanding the claim
Delete the related thresholds
questions.explanation: Missing validity evidence is not evidence of absence. The decision record should preserve unknowns instead of silently turning them into passes.

questions.question: Which control most directly reduces the risk that familiar benchmark questions masquerade as general knowledge?
options: Protect final items and check exact and near-duplicate overlap against available training, tuning, and retrieval data
Increase the number of colors in the dashboard
Use only one domain
Report no raw outputs
questions.explanation: Protected splits, provenance, and overlap analysis address known exposure. Fresh item families and controlled variants provide additional evidence.

questions.question: What is the most defensible conclusion from a suite that passes all predeclared support-assist gates?
options: The model has human-like understanding
The system knows every fact in the domain
The selected evidence supports the bounded support-assist use under the frozen protocol
Future versions will produce identical results
questions.explanation: Evaluation evidence supports a bounded interpretation and use. It does not establish unrestricted knowledge, human cognition, or future-version behavior.
